The investment case

How to use this report

Two separate questions Is SoFi becoming a better business? And does its share price leave enough room for things to go wrong? A growing company can still be an expensive investment. Start with the short conclusion below, then read the risks and valuation.

Read a number in context For each figure, ask what period it covers, whether it was reported or merely estimated, and what could change it. The numbered links show the evidence. A checklist status describes that criterion; it is not a buy or sell signal.

Limits of this reading The report uses June financial statements and the September 4 closing price. Some long-term history and peer comparisons remain incomplete. Beginner mode changes the explanation, not the figures, risks or assumptions. Experienced mode exposes the technical presentation. [129] [36] [10]

Terms explained
Revenue / net income

Revenue / net income Revenue measures business income; net income is what remains after recognized expenses and taxes. Bank net revenue already subtracts funding interest expense.

EPS

EPS Earnings per share: profit allocated to each share. More shares can mean slower EPS growth than total-profit growth. Diluted EPS accounts for relevant potential extra shares.

P/E

P/E Share price divided by annual earnings per share. A high multiple can reflect growth expectations; it also makes disappointing earnings more important.

ROE

ROE Profit divided by shareholders’ accounting equity. It measures profitability on that capital, not the stock-market return for an investor.

CET1

CET1 Core regulatory equity capital relative to risk-weighted assets. It indicates loss-absorbing capacity; it is neither a cash balance nor a guarantee against failure.

Book value / tangible book

Book value / tangible book Accounting assets minus liabilities gives equity or book value. Tangible book makes further adjustments for intangible assets. Neither is a guaranteed sale or liquidation value.

Dilution / stock compensation

Dilution / stock compensation Issuing new shares reduces the ownership percentage represented by an existing share. Paying employees with shares can avoid an immediate cash payment while still costing shareholders.

GAAP / adjusted

GAAP / adjusted GAAP uses the applicable accounting rules. Adjusted figures change selected items under the company’s definition; read what was changed before comparing them.

CAGR / TTM

CAGR / TTM CAGR is the constant annual growth rate connecting positive starting and ending values. TTM means the trailing twelve months. Neither term means a forecast.

Annualized

Annualized A shorter-period result expressed at a yearly pace. Multiplying a quarter’s profit by four does not prove the next four quarters will earn that amount.

Credit losses / fair value

Credit losses / fair value Borrowers may repay less than expected. Fair-value accounting estimates what loans are worth using assumptions, so changes in expected losses or discount rates can affect reported earnings.

CAPEX / operating cash flow / FCF

CAPEX / operating cash flow / FCF CAPEX is spending on long-lived assets. Operating cash flow measures cash in operating activities; free cash flow often subtracts cash CAPEX. Banks’ loan funding makes these industrial measures difficult to interpret.

Net interest margin / spread

Net interest margin / spread A bank earns interest and pays interest for funding. Net interest margin relates that difference to average interest-earning assets; it is not the final profit margin after all costs.

ROIC

ROIC A return measure commonly used for non-financial companies. For banks, debt and deposits are operating inputs, so the ordinary industrial formula can be misleading.

Discounted present value

Discounted present value Future value reduced to today’s equivalent using a required return. Changing profit, dilution, the final earnings multiple or the required return changes the result.

Margin of safety

Margin of safety The gap between the price paid and a cautious value estimate. A small gap leaves less room for estimation errors. The value estimate itself can still be wrong.

The business SoFi combines banking, loans and financial services in an app. Its revenue and profit are growing, but the technology business is shrinking. Growth alone therefore does not prove that every part of the company is working well. [01] [142] [144] [05]

The price The observed share price is $18.22. Our middle scenario estimates a present value of $19.65, only moderately higher. That is a conditional calculation, not a promised price: it needs strong profit growth and assumes investors will still pay a premium later. [129] [284] [275] [277]

What could go wrong Borrowers may fail to repay, funding may become more expensive, and new shares may reduce each existing share’s slice of future profits. SoFi has a substantial capital cushion today, but rapid lending growth is using some of it. These are the main checks before relying on the growth story. [06] [152] [84] [154]

01

Business quality SoFi is becoming a broader, profitable financial franchise. Distribution, cross-buy and deposit funding are strengths. A durable wide moat and high through-cycle returns are still unproven, particularly while the technology platform contracts. [01] [109] [112] [05] [161]

02

Price attractiveness At the September 4 close of $18.22, the shares trade at about 30× management’s FY26 adjusted EPS guide and 2.5× June tangible book. The base scenario offers only a modest present-value cushion; much of the value relies on sustained earnings growth and a premium terminal multiple. [129] [135] [136] [284] [311]

03

Strongest support Q2 GAAP revenue grew about 43% and net income about 61%. Cross-buy and a sizable deposit franchise support expansion. Revenue’s five-year CAGR easily exceeds the checklist hurdle. [142] [144] [109] [72] [35]

04

Strongest opposition Current group ROE is only about 5.9% annualized, dilution remains meaningful, and rapid loan growth is consuming capital. Credit marks, delinquent-loan sales and funding access deserve more weight than adjusted EBITDA alone. [161] [152] [154] [84] [06]

05

Read with the gaps All original sections and optional indicators are addressed. Missing long-run history, imperfect peer comparability and unverified market-positioning measures are visible throughout. Scenario values are assumptions-based estimates, not price targets or promised returns. [36] [208] [210] [311]

The full analysis

00What are we trying to find out?Preparation

Separate business growth from the result for one shareholder. The same company can grow while each share receives less of that growth if many new shares are issued. [148] [01]

Research separates the bank, fee businesses and software platform, then tests growth against per-share economics. [01] [04]

  • Is the market changing?Structural industry transformationMixed

    Financial services are moving toward apps and connected services. SoFi is gaining members, but adoption alone does not prove that these customers will be profitable. [107] [108] [01]

    Digital adoption supports the thesis, but a distinct 3–5-year structural-investment window has not been established. [01] [108]

    Full reasoning and evidence

    Digital distribution, integrated finance and outsourced banking infrastructure are changing how financial services are delivered. SoFi’s member growth and cross-buy show participation; secular adoption does not guarantee attractive credit-adjusted returns. [01] [107] [108] [109]

  • How complete is the evidence?Company and competitor researchMixed

    The filings and three peers were reviewed. Some long-run and cross-company comparisons are incomplete, so an unanswered question should stay unanswered rather than become a confident score. [36] [234] [236]

    Filings and three peers were reviewed. Investor Day/conference coverage and several peer comparisons remain incomplete. [01] [234]

    Full reasoning and evidence

    Audited annual statements, the latest quarterly filing, proxy, insider filings and three peers were inspected. Peer accounting, geography and ownership coverage are not fully harmonized; gaps are explicit rather than silently filled. [01] [234] [235] [236]

  • What is the first conclusion?Initial investment assessmentMixed

    The business is improving, but the price already needs substantial future success. Separate that conditional valuation from enthusiasm about customer growth. [311] [284]

    A credible growth franchise, with a modest base-case valuation cushion and meaningful credit and dilution risk. [311]

    Full reasoning and evidence

    Initial assessment: a credible growth franchise with improving profits, but current pricing needs continuing execution. High capital and rapid revenue growth coexist with low current group ROE and ongoing dilution. [311] [142] [161] [152]

    See section 8

    The original test asks for high, stable gross margins. A consolidated industrial gross margin is not meaningful for a deposit-funded lender. Use net interest margin and credit-adjusted net profitability; contribution margins exclude material corporate costs. [04] [50] [159]

  • Can we use the 10× interest-coverage test?Interest coverage above 10×Not applicable

    The original hurdle is interest coverage above 10×. For a bank, interest paid on deposits is a basic operating cost, making the industrial test misleading. It is not a pass; the relevant checks are capital, funding access and credit losses. [04] [53] [06]

    Original hurdle: interest coverage >10×. Deposit interest is operating funding, so this industrial ratio is not a valid bank test. [04] [53]

    Full reasoning and evidence

    The original interest coverage >10× criterion is inappropriate: deposit interest is an operating input and already reduces net revenue. An EBIT/interest ratio would distort bank economics.     Full reasoning and evidence

    The original net debt / FCF <4× criterion is not meaningful with bank operating funding and loan-driven negative CFO. It is neither calculated nor marked as passed. The relevant constraints are capital adequacy, deposit stability, eligible collateral and parent liquidity. [04] [96] [10] [192]

  • Is accounting profit the same as cash for owners?Free cash flow marginNot applicable

    No. Loan funding makes standard free-cash-flow margin unhelpful here, and bank capital limits distributions. The 2024 tax benefit also boosted accounting profit, so that year should not be treated as a fully recurring earnings base. [04] [10] [37]

    Bank CFO does not measure distributable owner cash. Assess earnings and capital generation, allowing for unusual tax effects. [04] [37] [132]

    See section 8
    Full reasoning and evidence

    A conventional FCF margin would be deeply negative because lending cash flows dominate CFO, but would not measure cash distributable to owners. GAAP net income and regulatory capital generation are better starting points. FY24 tax benefits also make a simple profit trend look smoother than recurring performance. [04] [188] [96] [37] [38] [132]

14What can the share-price history prove?Share-price history

Past price moves show volatility and past shareholder experience. They do not prove what comes next. Future results depend on earnings, credit quality and the price investors are willing to pay. [254] [311]

Public-market history has been volatile and has not matched the selected benchmarks over the audited comparison window. [254] [256] [258]

  • Does past price performance support the story?Historical performance and evidence for future runwayMixed

    In the filing’s June 2021–December 2025 comparison, $100 became $115.58 in SoFi, versus $175.08 in the Nasdaq benchmark. This is about 4.6 years, not a full five-year return or a current-date comparison. It describes past results, not future potential. [241] [246]

    SoFi lagged the chosen benchmarks over the audited return window. A further 5–10-year business runway remains conditional, not a price-history extrapolation. [254] [256] [258]

    Full reasoning and evidence

    The issuer’s reinvested-return graph shows a $100 June 1 2021 investment at $115.58 by December 31 2025, versus $175.08 for the Nasdaq Composite and $156.06 for S&P 500 Financials. This covers about 4.6 years, not a full five-year return. A 5–10-year business runway is plausible from digital adoption and cross-buy, but it is a conditional investment thesis rather than a historical-price extrapolation. A full current-date benchmark return series was not rebuilt. [241] [246] [251] [254] [256] [258] [107] [109]

What would change the thesis

  1. Growth and earnings Check the next results against FY26 guidance and the H2 profit requirement. A guide cut or revenue growth falling below the original 20% high-growth reference point would weaken the compounding case. [116] [117] [120] [173]

  2. Credit quality Track all-in loss estimates, delinquent-loan sales, vintage performance and fair-value assumptions together. Sustained deterioration from the Q2 all-in loss estimate would challenge the base scenario; reported charge-offs alone are insufficient. [06] [110] [103]

  3. Funding and capital Confirm October convertible principal funding and subsequent settlement. Track group and bank CET1, loan growth, deposit costs and facility eligibility. Continuing rapid capital-ratio decline would raise the probability of additional equity issuance. [91] [192] [84] [86] [154]

  4. Per-share economics Compare net-income growth with diluted EPS, actual share counts and total SBC including capitalized awards. Dilution above the base-model rate would lower per-share value unless incremental returns offset it. [276] [152] [171]

  5. Quality of growth Require a stabilization of technology revenue and accounts before assigning a stronger software moat. Cross-buy should eventually translate into better group ROE and measurable customer economics. [146] [05] [109] [161]

  6. New evidence Reassess acquisition returns, sweep litigation and the Payward rollout when quantified disclosures appear. No earnings contribution or loss estimate is invented before those disclosures. [09] [07] [08]

Open questions & data gaps

The full 14-section report is populated, but research remains partial: a ten-year comparable financial series, meaningful five-year P/E average and fully harmonized peer histories/ownership/capital were not verified. These gaps prevent a complete checklist pass. [36] [04]

Management’s all-in credit rate and guidance are estimates. Complete cohort loss curves, incremental cross-buy profitability, retention and a quantified technology-client recovery were not verified. [06] [05] [109]

Latest balance-sheet/share data are June 30, while market prices are September 4 closes. Post-quarter issuance and parent liquidity may differ. No live consolidated share count or unrestricted parent-only cash bridge was verified. [79] [129] [10]

Short interest has a settlement lag. Current comprehensive institutional flows, a consistent options put/call ratio, online attention and a complete technical study remain unverified. [206] [205] [208] [209] [210]

SEC filing index and smaller filings were accessible. Large SEC HTML downloads failed directly; full filings were downloaded from Yahoo Finance’s SEC-document mirror, with original accession links retained and the local source copies preserved. The mirrored figures were cross-checked against company results where material. Quote feeds also differ in auxiliary volume fields, so one identified session-volume series was retained. [40] [31] [129] [130]

04Use bank economics for the industrial checklistInformation available 5 Sep 2026Analytical judgment

04 Use bank economics for the industrial checklist

Use bank economics for the industrial checklist

Type
Analytical judgment
Period
Information available 5 Sep 2026
Unit
qualitative
Basis
Analytical assessment

Deposits and much borrowing are operating funding; lending flows dominate CFO. Ordinary gross margin, industrial ROIC, EBITDA/interest and net-debt/FCF are not reliable scores here. Use net interest margin, credit-adjusted profitability, group ROE, tangible book value, CET1 and liquidity instead. Sector adjustments preserve the original checklist thresholds rather than claiming they have been passed.

06Credit metrics need sales and seasoning adjustmentsInformation available 5 Sep 2026Analytical judgment

06 Credit metrics need sales and seasoning adjustments

Credit metrics need sales and seasoning adjustments

Type
Analytical judgment
Period
Information available 5 Sep 2026
Unit
qualitative
Basis
Analytical assessment

Reported personal-loan charge-offs exclude losses realized through late-stage delinquency sales. Management also provides an estimated all-in annualized rate. Neither measure is a lifetime loss rate; loan growth can suppress annualized ratios before new vintages season. Most personal/student loans use fair value, so credit costs also appear in valuation and sale income rather than only the provision line.

234Happen is the closest US personal-loan benchmarkInformation available 5 Sep 2026Analytical judgment

234 Happen is the closest US personal-loan benchmark

Happen is the closest US personal-loan benchmark

Type
Analytical judgment
Period
Information available 5 Sep 2026
Unit
qualitative
Basis
Analytical assessment

LendingClub became Happen in June 2026 and now trades as HAPN. Its prime personal-loan marketplace and deposits overlap most directly. Scott Sanborn’s team operates a narrower franchise. Q2 revenue rose modestly; new fair-value accounting and a provision benefit support reported profit, limiting a clean operating comparison. Capital-return activity contrasts with SoFi issuance.

Founder-led Nu is a profitability and customer-scale comparator in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia, not a direct US personal-loan competitor. Its FX, regulation and credit mix differ materially. 311Improving business; modest base-case valuation cushionInformation available 5 Sep 2026Analytical judgment

311 Improving business; modest base-case valuation cushion

Improving business; modest base-case valuation cushion

Type
Analytical judgment
Period
Information available 5 Sep 2026
Unit
qualitative
Basis
Analytical assessment

At the observed price the shares require sustained per-share earnings growth. The base case supports only a limited present-value cushion, and both the earnings path and terminal premium matter. Strong capital today does not prove high through-cycle returns or eliminate the need for future equity issuance.
